$comment: DERIVED, not verbatim. Written by this library from the prose of the W3C Recommendation Verifiable Credential Data Integrity 1.0 (REC-vc-data-integrity-20250515), which prints no JSON Schema, CDDL or ABNF of its own (README.md gives the search). Source .cache/w3c-vc-data-integrity-1-0.bin, sha256 ba5c4baf13fe3bab3ebd95ab6650d6fe83720e254b383bb444b4fbbae7bcf4fe; quotations are cut from its rendering .cache/w3c-vc-data-integrity-1-0.txt, sha256 2b7725f80e138ef943eff25050eee6a62f8887762ca9e1e03867c55ea5647beb, and cite its line numbers (L). LEVELS: the root and every anchor not ending in -should state MUST and MUST NOT rules, so a failure there is non-conformance; an anchor ending in -should adds SHOULD statements and includes the root by reference, so a failure there is a warning. MAY statements are never constraints: a leniency a MAY grants has its own anchor, named for the leniency. A constraint marked INFERRED is a reading this library made, not a statement of the source; one marked OUTSIDE-SOURCE comes from a document the source names and is not this source's. Rule ids (P-nn, S-nn, V-nn, E-nn, O-nn, M-nn) are those of rules.derived.yaml. INSTANCE: a ProblemDetails map [RFC9457] that carries a Data Integrity error (section 4.7). ROOT = MUST: type is a URL that starts with https://w3id.org/security# and ends with one of the five values section 4.7 lists. ANCHORS: #with-referenced-names (also PARSING_ERROR and DATA_LOSS_DETECTION_ERROR, which sections 2.4.3 and 4.4 name and 4.7 does not define: README T-04), #problem-details-should (SHOULD: title and detail present as strings). The five names are I-14. Members RFC 9457 defines and this source does not mention (status, instance) are allowed.
title: A ProblemDetails map carrying a Data Integrity error (DERIVED)

type.$comment: E-01 w3c-vc-data-integrity-1-0#R-0273: “The type value of the error object MUST be a URL that starts with the value https://w3id.org/security# and ends with the value in the section listed below.” (L663) The section lists five: PROOF_GENERATION_ERROR, PROOF_VERIFICATION_ERROR, PROOF_TRANSFORMATION_ERROR, INVALID_DOMAIN_ERROR, INVALID_CHALLENGE_ERROR. Applies only where “If [RFC9457] is used:” (L662) holds, which the root takes as the instance being a ProblemDetails map.

referenced.$comment: ANCHOR #with-referenced-names. E-02: PARSING_ERROR (w3c-vc-data-integrity-1-0#R-0221, L601) and DATA_LOSS_DETECTION_ERROR (w3c-vc-data-integrity-1-0#R-0142, L452) are named as error types the algorithms SHOULD convey, and section 4.7 defines neither, so the MUST of E-01 read literally excludes the type URLs of two errors the source asks for. This anchor admits them.

should.$comment: ANCHOR #problem-details-should. SHOULD level, includes the root. E-03 w3c-vc-data-integrity-1-0#R-0077: “The title value SHOULD provide a short but specific human-readable string for the error.” (L664) E-04 w3c-vc-data-integrity-1-0#R-0078: “The detail value SHOULD provide a longer human-readable string for the error.” (L665) w3c-vc-data-integrity-1-0#R-0075: “implementers SHOULD use [RFC9457] to encode the error data structure as a ProblemDetails map” (L662). Non-empty: INFERRED from short and longer human-readable string.
